name: Revanesse

card.summary: A Canadian range of hyaluronic acid dermal fillers (Prollenium) used to restore volume and reshape lips, chin and cheeks.
card.aka: Prollenium HA filler; Revanesse Versa, Ultra, Lips
card.note: Injected by licensed clinicians; complications can occur.

quick.overview:
Revanesse is a line of cross-linked hyaluronic acid fillers made by Prollenium. Different versions are used for lips, fine lines and deeper volume.

A 15-person study of Revanesse Ultra found good volume restoration at 24 weeks with no adverse events, and a 40-woman chin study with Revanesse Versa reported satisfaction sustained to six months.
quick.how: A clinician injects the gel with needle or cannula into targeted areas. Results appear almost immediately and are temporary, with hyaluronidase available to dissolve HA filler.
quick.risks: Filler risks include swelling, bruising and, rarely, vascular complications. Laboratory work rates Revanesse Versa/Lips as moderately resistant to hyaluronidase.

lead: Revanesse is a range of hyaluronic acid dermal fillers made by Prollenium, a Canadian company. Clinicians inject them to restore volume, smooth lines or shape features such as lips and chin.[1][2]
Published research includes a 24-week clinical evaluation of Revanesse Ultra in 15 subjects with moderate volume loss, and a study of Revanesse Versa for chin augmentation.[1][2]

chain: HA gel injected into targeted areas
angle.text: Revanesse fillers add volume to lips, cheeks, folds or chin. Results are visible straight away and fade as the gel is absorbed.

paras: A 24-week study of 15 adults (mean age about 48.5) with moderate volume loss used Revanesse Ultra and found marked facial volume restoration on the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale, no reported adverse events and satisfaction in all patients.[1] In a study of 40 women with small chins, Revanesse Versa placed with a cannula in multiple layers raised satisfaction at 14 days, maintained to six months.[2]

In vitro, Revanesse Versa/Lips was in the moderately resistant group among 21 HA fillers tested with recombinant human hyaluronidase.[3] Another bench study measured extrusion force across fillers including Revanesse Versa, finding it between less and more forceful products.[4]
